tasks.short: Work out and select the lumber and other materials a job needs, order them and check the delivery.

steps.what: Carpenter reads drawings and measures on site to work out quantities
Carpenter selects lumber, sheets and fixings and writes the material list

loop.input: A photo of the carpenter's handwritten additions to the pre-filled material list.
loop.output: Article codes and quantities matched to the merchant's catalogue.
loop.check: Every code must exist in the catalogue data; quantities must be numbers in the article's unit; lines with no confident match go to the carpenter unmatched.
loop.stop: One pass per photo; unmatched lines are typed by the carpenter.
loop.why_not_simpler: Handwritten site lists use trade shorthand and sizes that a lookup table cannot read.

steps.what: Carpenter checks what is already in the van or the yard
Work planner checks the list against the job budget and approves
Carpenter orders the materials from the timber merchant by phone, app or e-mail
Carpenter receives or collects the delivery and unloads it on site
Carpenter checks the delivery against the order

tasks.design: The {ERP} pre-fills the material list from the job calculation with catalogue article codes; the carpenter adjusts it after measuring, and a bounded model step reads handwritten additions into article codes. Once the work planner approves in the app, the order goes electronically to the merchant through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}, and the delivery is ticked off on the phone against the same order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site lists were handwritten and phoned in, because calculations and catalogues lived in the office.
tasks.enabler_now: Construction ERPs capture materials on site and order electronically, and the sector shares product and price data that order software connects to.
tasks.still_hard: Measuring and choosing timber quality on site stay with the carpenter; site changes outrun the calculation.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what the job really needs once the old structure is opened up, and choosing wood that will hold.

ambition.what: Material use compared with the calculation on every job, so estimates improve job by job.

tasks.altitude: The carpenter adjusts and confirms orders instead of phoning them in; the work planner approves from the app.

reach.task: Collect and check materials on site
reach.learn: Whether delivery ticking on the phone finds short deliveries.

evidence.claim: An ERP for installation firms captures materials on site and handles material ordering and call-off.
A Dutch product and price data hub for the installation sector feeds order software.
A construction ERP handles purchase orders with invoice recognition.

assumptions: Boundary: from measuring to the delivery checked; storage and use on site are outside.
Input contract: job calculation with quantities per article, produced by the estimator in the {ERP}; merchant catalogue with article codes and prices; fallback is a phoned order.
Native configuration is tried first: the ERP's site ordering before custom code.
Work planner time is outside the carpenter's savings.
Collecting and unloading (s6) keep their full time; only the check against the order (s7) is priced, at what ticking off order lines on the phone removes.
unknowns: Whether the timber merchant accepts electronic orders.
How often site lists differ from the calculation.
research_questions: How much wasted timber comes from ordering errors today?

already_counted.description: Carpenter checks the pre-filled list and the read article codes.

incremental.description: Carpenter fixes unmatched articles and failed orders.
Estimator keeps calculation article codes aligned with the catalogue.

approvals.approved_version: Material list with articles and quantities as approved by the work planner in s4; changes need a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Renovation jobs where most materials are decided on site gain little from the calculation, and merchants without electronic ordering keep the phone.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange heating, electrical and other subcontractors: book them, agree scope and dates, and coordinate on site.

steps.what: Lead carpenter identifies work needing subcontractors and when it is due
Lead carpenter phones subcontractors to check availability and price
Lead carpenter agrees scope and dates with the subcontractor
Lead carpenter sends the construction drawings to the subcontractor
Site manager approves the subcontract scope and price
Office administrator issues the subcontract order
Lead carpenter coordinates site access, sequence and readiness with subcontractors
Lead carpenter checks the heating or electrical work is done before closing in

tasks.design: A project planning board in the {PROJECT} or {ERP} planning app shows subcontractor slots, and regular subcontractors confirm availability through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}. A scope template per trade pulls drawings from the {DOCS} store, the approved scope becomes the subcontract order, and readiness notices go out automatically when the preceding work is marked done.
tasks.previous_blocker: Subcontracting ran on phone calls and chat threads, and the order was retyped by the office.
tasks.enabler_now: Construction planning apps and partner portals share slots and documents, and order templates fill from approved scopes.
tasks.still_hard: Small subcontractors work by phone; good subcontractors are scarce and dates slip.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which subcontractor will turn up and do good work, and sorting out clashes on site.

ambition.what: Subcontractor slots reviewed weekly against site progress, so closing-in is never held up by a missed booking.

tasks.altitude: The lead carpenter spends less time on the phone and more on site coordination; the site manager approves from a filled scope.

reach.task: Plan installation work around the carpentry
reach.learn: Whether readiness notices give electricians enough warning.

evidence.claim: A construction ERP plans staff and equipment in an app.
Construction management software keeps site diaries, defect logs and checklists.
Main contractors carry chain liability for subcontractors' wage taxes; details follow national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from identifying subcontracted work to checking it before closing in; invoicing is outside.

Input contract: project schedule with trade tasks, kept by the work planner; preferred subcontractor list with trades and rates, kept by the site manager; drawings in the {DOCS} store; fallback is the phone.
Site manager and office time is outside the lead carpenter's savings.
Checking the work before closing in does not change.
unknowns: Whether regular subcontractors would use a portal.
How many subcontracts a carpenter arranges per month.
research_questions: How often does closing-in wait for a subcontractor today?

already_counted.description: Lead carpenter checks the filled scope template before sending.

incremental.description: Lead carpenter keeps task status current so readiness notices fire.
Site manager keeps scope templates and the subcontractor list current.

approvals.approved_version: Subcontract scope with trade, dates and price as approved by the site manager in s4; changes need a new approval.
The drawings for the scope agreed by the lead carpenter in s3; a changed scope needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Where subcontractors are small firms who only answer the phone, availability checks stay manual.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the work crew, tell crew members their jobs, and keep job records of hours and materials.

steps.what: Foreman plans the work crew for the week on a whiteboard or spreadsheet
Foreman messages each crew member where and when to work
Crew members write hours and materials on paper timesheets
Foreman checks timesheets and writes the daily job records

loop.input: The foreman's voice note about the day's progress and problems.
loop.output: Checklist fields for the job and a short draft remark.
loop.check: Fields are validated against the job checklist; every item to be closed in needs a photo; numbers must match logged hours.
loop.stop: One pass per note; the foreman confirms or types it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Spoken site notes are free text; a form alone makes the foreman type on site.

steps.what: Office administrator types hours and materials into the ERP

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP}'s planning board and mobile app: the foreman plans the crew by skills and availability, crew members see their jobs and log hours and materials per job in the app. The foreman approves the day's hours in the app, a voice note becomes checklist fields and a remark through a bounded model step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site work ran on paper timesheets and phone calls, and the office retyped everything.
tasks.enabler_now: Construction ERPs plan crews and log hours and materials in an app.
tasks.still_hard: Crews must log consistently; logs per worker touch privacy and works council rights.
tasks.human_edge: Matching people to tasks they do well and sensing when the crew is overloaded.

ambition.what: Job cost against budget visible every day instead of after the invoice run.

tasks.altitude: The foreman approves logged hours instead of collecting paper; planning decisions stay theirs.

reach.task: Log hours and materials on site
reach.learn: Whether laborers log reliably in the app without reminders.

evidence.claim: A construction ERP plans staff and equipment in an app and logs hours there.
About 200 handhelds replaced paper work orders at a sewer cleaning firm; orders per day rose from 1,500-1,600 to about 2,000 with payback in six months (director's figures, 2009).
A project manager reports saving about 10 hours a week on site diaries, defects and acceptance (self-reported, vendor-published).
Hours, location and job logs per fitter observe presence and performance and need works council consent.
Rule-based scheduling on skills and distance is not high-risk AI; a model ranking workers on speed would be.

assumptions: Boundary: from planning the crew to the job record; progress reporting and payroll are outside.

Input contract: crew availability and skills kept by the foreman in the planning app; hours and materials per job logged by crew members; job checklist set by the work planner; fallback is paper timesheets.
Crew logging time replaces their paper timesheets and stays outside the foreman's savings.
No location tracking of vans or people is added.
unknowns: Whether the company's ERP has a planning board and mobile app licensed.
Whether the works council has agreed to app-based hours.
research_questions: How many hours a week does the office spend retyping timesheets today?

already_counted.description: Foreman reviews logged hours and the daily job record before approving.

incremental.description: Foreman chases crew members who forget to log and fixes wrong job codes.
Work planner keeps job codes and checklists current.

approvals.approved_version: The day's hours and materials per job as approved by the foreman in s4; corrections reopen approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If crew members log late or wrongly, the foreman keeps chasing and correcting, which eats much of the paperwork saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Dig or direct digging of post holes and set poles to support structures, after checking for buried cables.

steps.what: Carpenter files the excavation notice for cable and pipe maps of the site
Carpenter reads the cable map and marks out post holes on site
Carpenter digs or directs digging of the post holes
Carpenter sets and plumbs poles and fixes them to support structures
Carpenter reports any damaged cable or pipe to the owner and the office

tasks.design: The excavation notice is pre-filled from the job address and drawing in the work order of the {ERP} and filed on the {GOV_PORTAL}; the returned cable and pipe map opens on the phone at the location. Digging and setting poles do not change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Little blocked it; the notice is short, and the work is physical.
tasks.enabler_now: Work orders hold the address and site plan that the notice needs.
tasks.still_hard: Digging, plumbing and fixing poles are hands-on; maps can be inaccurate, so hand digging near cables stays.
tasks.human_edge: Reading the ground and setting a pole true and solid.

reach.task: Dig trenches and holes on site
reach.learn: Whether the pre-filled notice suits all digging on the job.

evidence.claim: A work order in a construction ERP holds the job address and site documents.
Mechanical digging requires an excavation notice and the cable and pipe maps on site; details follow national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the excavation notice to poles set; building the structure on the poles is outside.
Input contract: job address and site plan, produced by the work planner in the {ERP} work order; fallback is filing the notice by hand.
Upkeep: the carpenter checks the job address in the work order, about half an hour per 100 baseline hours.
unknowns: Who files excavation notices in the company today.
How often post holes are dug by machine.
research_questions: How often do maps differ from what is found in the ground?

incremental.description: Carpenter checks the work order address and site plan before filing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Jobs where the office already files notices leave nothing to save; the physical work dominates.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The carpenter keeps measuring, building and judging materials on site; phoned orders, paper timesheets and retyped records shrink.
reach: Construction laborers' hours and material logging
skills_to_grow: Logging hours and progress in the job app
Using planning boards to coordinate subcontractors
role.ambitious_version: A carpenter-foreman who sees job cost against budget daily and keeps crew, materials and subcontractors in step from a phone.
